semantic_correction.stem: During admission, a nurse identifies a wound on a client's lower leg. Which documentation is most appropriate?

options.A: Document the wound's location and photograph, then defer measurements and drainage description until the next dressing change unless the wound appears infected.
options.B: Document the wound's dimensions and current dressing, then omit wound-bed and surrounding-skin findings because those details are more relevant to treatment than baseline assessment.
options.C: Record that a lower-leg wound is present and complete the detailed description at the first scheduled dressing change so later measurements can serve as the baseline.
options.D: Document the precise location, length, width and depth as indicated, wound-bed and edge findings, periwound skin, drainage, pain, and signs of infection or other relevant findings.

semantic_correction.rationale: D is correct. Current NCBI/Open RN Nursing Skills guidance states that wound assessment and documentation should include anatomic location, wound type when known, degree of tissue damage, wound bed, wound size, wound edges and periwound skin, signs of infection, and pain. Drainage should be described by color, consistency, and amount. The same source states that wounds should be measured on admission and during subsequent dressing changes so healing can be compared accurately over time. Therefore a comprehensive baseline description should be recorded when the wound is identified on admission. A is incomplete because it delays measurements and drainage description. B is incomplete because wound-bed and periwound findings are core assessment data. C is incorrect because postponing the baseline description until a later dressing change loses the admission comparison point.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Document a wound comprehensively at baseline using precise location, measurements, wound-bed and periwound characteristics, drainage, pain, and signs of infection so later assessments can be compared accurately.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed absolute-word and answer-length cueing, rebuilt all four documentation choices to comparable length and specificity, freshly verified current NCBI/Open RN wound-assessment guidance, and preserved comprehensive admission documentation as the single best response.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests comprehensive baseline wound documentation with one clearly best answer, balanced alternatives, current source verification, and no absolute-word or length cue.

option_audit.A: Incorrect. It omits and delays baseline measurements and drainage findings that should be documented when the wound is assessed.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Wound-bed and periwound findings are core components of wound assessment and documentation.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Wounds should be measured on admission so later assessments can be compared with the true baseline.
option_audit.D: Correct. It captures the core wound-assessment elements identified in current NCBI/Open RN guidance.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. D uniquely provides a complete baseline assessment; A and B omit core data, and C delays the baseline until a later encounter.
cueing_check: All four options are parallel documentation approaches of comparable length and specificity; prior absolute-word distractors and uniquely-long-answer cueing were removed.
